content: The Sine oculis-binding protein homolog (SOBP), also referred to as Jackson circler protein 1 (JXC1), is a protein encoded by the SOBP gene in humans. The SOBP gene was first identified in Drosophila melanogaster through a yeast two-hybrid screen that utilized the SIX domain of the Sine oculis protein as bait. In most genomes containing the SOBP gene, it exists as a single copy. In humans, the SOBP gene is located on the long arm of chromosome 6 at position 6q21, spanning a physical distance of slightly more than 171 kilobase pairs (kbp). The mRNA is transcribed from seven exons, oriented from centromere to telomere, with the first six exons forming the open reading frame. The coding mRNA consists of 2,622 nucleotides, encoding a protein of 873 amino acids. In mice, the Sopb gene is located on chromosome 10 at cytogenetic band 10qB2, covering a physical region of 172 kbp. Similar to humans, the mouse Sopb coding region spans six exons, but its open reading frame is slightly shorter, comprising 2,595 nucleotides that encode a protein of 864 amino acids. The SOBP protein contains two nuclear localization signals, one at the amino terminus and the other at the carboxy terminus. It also features two proline-rich sequences and two domains related to the FCS-type zinc finger domain. Additionally, all SOBP proteins share two highly conserved motifs. In mice, gene expression profiling using RT-PCR has demonstrated a broad expression pattern in both adult and embryonic tissues, with the highest expression observed in the brain. RNA in-situ hybridization has shown that Sopb is expressed in neonatal tissues, including the spiral ganglion, sensory and supporting cells of the maculae of the saccule and utricle, and the cristae ampullaris. It is also expressed in the inner nuclear layer of the developing retina at embryonic day 15 (E15), the olfactory epithelium, neurons of the trigeminal ganglion, and cells surrounding the dermal papillae of hair follicles. In humans, an autosomal recessive mutation in the SOBP gene causes a condition known as MRAMS syndrome (OMIM 613671), characterized by severe intellectual disability, anterior maxillary protrusion, and strabismus. This mutation is located within an 8 Mbp region on 6q21. Analysis of candidate genes within this interval identified a homozygous missense mutation in SOBP in patients with MRAMS syndrome. In mice, two independent spontaneous autosomal recessive mutations, named Jackson circler (jc) and jc2J, were identified at The Jackson Laboratory. Genetic linkage analyses localized these mutations to chromosome 10. Molecular genetic studies revealed a small 10 base pair deletion in exon 6 of the Sopb gene, leading to a frameshift in the open reading frame and the introduction of a stop codon at amino acid position 490 (S449fsX490). The truncating mutations jc and jc2J in mice result in profound hearing loss and erratic circling behavior. Specifically, the cochlear duct is shortened, and the organ of Corti exhibits abnormalities such as supernumerary outer hair cells, mirror image duplications of the tunnel of Corti and inner hair cells, and ectopic patches of vestibular-like hair cells in Kolliker's organ. The vestibular end organs are also smaller in surface area and thicker.
